title: I Took the CNC-Mill Reservation to the Mentor Who Left a Toolpath Running

parts.text: I loaded stock at 3:02 p.m. and mentor Jax's toolpath was still cutting on my reserved mill. The screen said: END JOB ON THE BEEP. NINETY MINUTES. UNLOAD. I was thirty-one, night student, holding a reservation. Jax did not unload. "Mentors are the spindle." I photographed the screen, the reservation, and his still-green cycle. Then I logged a leftover job. At 3:10 the shop lead asked why Jax's cycle was on my ninety. I let them finish the sentence they would regret in writing. Petty is a word people use when their name is on the ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shop lead can see Jax's green cycle on the mill during my reserved ninety.

social.video_title: He left a toolpath running into my mill slot — Part 1/2
social.description: CNC mill, a reservation, and a mentor's leftover cycle. I logged the leftover. Would you have waited for the beep?

parts.text: Jax called it a finish until the lead asked for the log. I printed the leftover, the photo, and the screen. The job ended. Jax reserved finish time and told students finishes were always about optics. Optics is a word mentors use when a cycle exists. Reservation now has a second line: MENTORS UNLOAD. I keep my ninety. Jax books. The mill finally cuts a file, not a leftover. Nobody thanked me, which is how you know a policy finally works. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.

social.description: Leftover log, ended cycle, and a second line. Was a finish ever my stock?
